answers:
Lane: objective (measurement and sizing). Classification of readings 1 to 6:
- Reading 1 is a read cost.
- Readings 2, 3, 4, and 5 are budgets.
- Reading 6 is a window.
Reading 2 is a test timeout that backs up budgeted rows. Reading 3 is a table timeout plus the tip settle budgets. Reading 4 is an animation settle budget. Reading 5 is a per-press scroll settle with structural termination.

The ruling entries give each reading's property, signal, and sizing. Every figure follows rule R: slowest queued reading × max(618.6/494.0 = 1.252, the reading's own spread), rounded up. It is recorded as a constant whose comment names the runs, and is re-derived when a timing entry exceeds bound ÷ margin.

Alternative rejected: a budget computed at run time from a calibration settle. It would scale with the very regression it has to catch.

Yes: 5 ms plus one frame is the right refusal window when motion is off. The 5 ms is the engine's completion pad (helpers.ts:935-945; documented at setupBrowser.ts:3432). Any state change a refusal starts under reduced motion runs on that same pad, and that pad was queued before the observer's AbortSignal.timeout (:3515).

The late mutation comes from the static bounce:
- `modal-static` is added synchronously (Modal.ts:244) and removed after the first pad (Modal.ts:247-251). That removal is a class record.
- The overflowY writes (:243, :254) touch `style`, which the filter at :3519-3527 ignores.
- `element.focus()` (:248) writes no attribute.
- Trap.ts writes no attribute or class.
- #prevent writes no aria-* attribute.

The defect is in the act. actOnOverlayControl treats hidePrevented as completion (:5164-5179). Under reduced motion nothing animates, so waitForAnimations(host) (:5180) returns at once. One frame (:5181) can then elapse before the 5 ms pad fires, which leaves the removal inside the observation. Motion=true passes because waitForAnimations re-reads after each finish and so covers both bounce transitions (index.js:1308-1310).

The observer cannot wait for an engine completion signal: the bounce emits none (Modal.ts:232-257). The act must instead settle on the predicate 'hidePrevented recorded and host lacks modal-static'.

Alternatives rejected:
- Filtering `modal-static` out of the observer would hide a stuck class.
- Widening the window is a clock under load.

The previous state's panel is not the source. buildJourney (integration.test.ts:1248) calls buildShowcase, then destroyShowcase (setupBrowser.ts:1398-1404, :1494-1500), which destroys journeyVeneer. Tip.destroy then removes the panel synchronously (Tip.ts:267-292).

The stray, three elements the size of a tooltip panel, arises inside the tooltip state's own act. The act clicks a Contents link and tabs to the trigger, so it might come from a focus pass or from a hover after the jump.

It is the usual case, not a rare one:
- The 390 tooltip rows read 10766 in 15 of 18 rows across nine runs.
- They read 10763 only in jb2b-1 light, jb2b-2 light, and after-4 dark.
- Every 1280 tooltip row reads 10763.
The J-B2 pair itself holds a race outcome: light 10763 and dark 10766 in both runs.

Where to wait: after the open (:1265-1267) and the binding (:1278-1308), and before the count (:1317). Park the pointer (setupBrowser.ts:3256), then wait until no connected tip panel or backdrop outside the bound set remains. Waiting before buildJourney cannot see a stray that the act itself creates.

Why a connection predicate: `hidden.bs.tooltip` fires after disposal (Tip.ts:322-324). A re-hovered tip keeps its panel connected through that event, so the event does not prove the panel left.

Keep `excluded` in the row. It is a count, and with the predicate it is deterministic: 10763 at both widths. A leaked engine panel changes it, which is a defect the row exists to catch. Moving it to the Journal changes nothing, because the Journal is compared too (compare.ts:536-547). Giving it a timing key would hide a leak. Counting only the owned elements already exists: that is `signatures`.

Yes: each table carries its own bound, as a `timeout` property on its COMPONENT_TABLES row.

The shared formula at integration.test.ts:2112 gives every table the bound implied by the largest scenario count (230 s). Popover's margin is therefore incidental. Scenario count alone cannot size a table, because per-row cost depends on family and motion. Measured across the seven queued runs:
- popover motion=true: 62.1-165.8 s
- popover motion=false: 10.8-13.3 s
- scrollspy-390 motion=false: 62.2-75.1 s
- modal motion=true: 37.8-42.7 s

The bound is a measured property: rule R applied to that table's report.json durations, bounding its slower motion run.

Vitest applies one timeout to a whole it.each. Register each row with it.each([row]) and the same title template, so titles and the host-bound gate stay byte-identical.

Popover motion=true has a spread of 2.67 that does not track wall time. U4's per-row entries must locate that spread before its figure lands.

Yes: waitForAnimations must take a budget, and the library already accepts one (options.budget, index.js:1329-1331).

The 774.5 ms reading at :3199 cannot size it:
- It was a scroll settle, not an animation settle.
- It came from the j0c2 diagnostic runs (305.69 and 319.32 s walls, 66 tests; /home/user/veneer/tmp/codex/j0c4-history.md:26), outside this band and this suite.
- The comment names no run.
The 5,000 ms built on it is a comfort figure (tmp/units/journey-cost/evidence/design-folder/measure.md:219).

The after-3b failure shows a `transform` transition still running at 1000.5 ms in a 562.0 s run. Re-derive one COMPONENT_WAIT from the U5 per-wait probe by rule R; the property and the load are the same for conditions and animations. The margin property: the larger of the band spread (1.252) and the settle's own spread, so the budget admits a run as far above the slowest settle as the band itself spreads. The budget must also stay below each table's slack, so an exhausted wait names its condition before Vitest's timeout.

Neither. The 8-poll settle is a clock in disguise: 8 × the 10 ms default interval of unchanged scrollTop (core index.js:241). A press whose scroll starts late passes it.

The after-3b failure shows this. The message reads top=160, height=255, extent=1378, so the region could still move; the predicate ended before the scroll did.

The press must instead end on the browser's `scrollend` event on the region, armed before the press and only when the region can move in the key's direction. Two frames follow so the IntersectionObserver notification lands (Scrollspy.ts:52, :114-130).

The activation event is not a per-press signal. It fires only when the selection changes (Scrollspy.ts:167), and the act already asserts it (setupBrowser.ts:5701, :5719).

The 100-press bound has no measurement behind it. Replace it with structural termination: each press must move scrollTop toward the key's boundary, or the loop throws `cannot reach`.

Every reading is a veneer test-layer change: tests/setupBrowser.ts, tests/setupBrowser.test.ts, tests/app/browser/integration.test.ts, tests/app/browser/Showcase.test.ts, and tests/integration.test.ts.

@orkestrel/test/browser: no change. waitForAnimations accepts a budget (index.js:1329-1331), and waitForEvent exists for scrollend (core index.js:429-461). Changing the 1,000 ms default would change every consumer's contract to suit one host's load, so refuse it.

Engine (stage B): no change.
- Tips already emit `hidden.bs.<profile>` after the panel is disposed (Tip.ts:322-324; constants.ts:155, :162). The brief's 'phase getter only' premise omits that event, and the reader needs a connection predicate either way.
- The modal bounce has no completion event (Modal.ts:232-257), but its class removal is an observable settle predicate. Adding an event would be product surface with no consumer that needs it.

Two items outside the code: the records to amend are listed under risks, and the units follow in order U1 to U7.
